answer: One concrete defense is per-identity admission proof-of-work: before an identity can earn, it must solve a fresh computational puzzle that takes minutes of real compute and cannot be copied to another identity. Think of it as a spiral climb: each fake identity must climb separately, and no lotus blooms without that climb. Established standing then only grows from later graded work. An attacker who wants 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times that compute and time, so the cost rises linearly to a summit that honest users, who pay once, can afford but a farm cannot hide.
